adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the verifier cannot find English source files for community resources, but examining the diff shows the path transformation `replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` is designed to map community translation files to their English counterparts in the main resources directory. Looking at the actual file structure in the diff, English files exist at paths like `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/messages/messages_en.properties` which would be correctly found by this transformation for community files at `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_*.properties`. The transformation also handles the `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` to `_en.properties` conversion. The verifier logic appears sound for the intended use case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:74 — [P1, confidence 100, anchor 74] `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` rewrites each changed `themes/src/main/resources-community/...` bundle to a nonexistent `themes/src/main/resources/.../messages_en.properties`, so the `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` at lines 76-79 throws an unwrapped `RuntimeException` and aborts verification instead of reporting the affected bundle.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at line 74 replaces 'resources-community' with 'resources' to find the English file. Looking at the diff, files like 'themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_fi.properties' would be transformed to look for an English file at 'themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/account/messages/messages_en.properties'. However, examining the diff structure, the English base files exist at paths like 'themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/messages/messages_en.properties' (shown in the diff), so the path transformation appears correct for the main resources. But for community-only translations where no corresponding English file exists in the resources folder, the FileInputStream would throw an IOException wrapped in RuntimeException, aborting verification. The code does not handle the case where the English reference file doesn't exist gracefully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:46 — P1 (confidence 100, anchor: XSS enforcement): `public List<String> verify() throws MojoExecutionException {` is only called by unit tests and no Mojo/build configuration invokes it, so a malicious HTML-bearing translation can be merged and shipped without the new sanitizer ever detecting it.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims verify() is only called by unit tests and no Mojo/build configuration invokes it. However, looking at the diff, this is a Maven plugin (VerifyMessageProperties is in misc/theme-verifier which has a pom.xml). The class extends or is used by a Mojo (imports MojoExecutionException). The diff shows this is an existing verification tool being enhanced with HTML sanitization. The finding assumes the tool isn't integrated into the build, but the diff doesn't show the Mojo configuration - it only shows the verifier class itself. The tool already existed (verifyNoDuplicateKeys was already being called), and the new verifySafeHtml() is added to the same verify() method. Without seeing the full project structure, we cannot verify the claim that it's never invoked during builds. The existing test infrastructure and the nature of the changes suggest this is a build-time verification tool.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java:50 — P2 (confidence 100): `List<String> verify = getFile("changedAnchor_de.properties").verify();` covers only the mismatched-anchor rejection path, so a regression that rejects or flags anchors exactly matching the English source will still pass without verifying the newly intended allow path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test `verifyNoChangedAnchors` only tests the rejection case (when anchors don't match). Looking at the diff, the `santizeAnchors` method in VerifyMessageProperties.java has logic to allow anchors that exactly match between source and target (the `if (englishMatcher.find() && Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group()))` branch). However, there's no test verifying that matching anchors are properly allowed/passed through. The test file `changedAnchor_de.properties` has a different URL than `changedAnchor_en.properties` (malicious.com vs example.com), so it only tests the rejection path. A test for the happy path (matching anchors being allowed) would be valuable for this new functionality.
